answer: Reviewers post stake before scoring, and the protocol re-grades roughly one in twenty scores against a hidden reference. A score that diverges costs the reviewer the stake, which makes rubber-stamping pricier than reading. Standing expires unless renewed by fresh work each epoch, so an operator who spins up ten thousand relic accounts and walks away watches them drop off the island alone. Keeping them alive needs ten thousand fresh submissions an epoch; that mirror is what a real operator's output actually looks like.
